3DRS · renderer rewrite

3DRS Graphics Overhaul

The same maps, saves and blocky characters, drawn by a new HDR pipeline. There are still no image or model files: every surface, cloud, flame and blade of grass is generated in code. Drag across each picture to compare the old renderer with the new one.

  • No texture files
  • 4 shadow cascades
  • ~58 grass blades per m²
  • 2,077 trees in the wilderness
  • ~52 FPS uncapped, castle view

Before and after

These are the repository's fixed lighting-audit viewpoints. Both builds use the same save and camera. The game's clock is a day fraction, so set_time 0.50 is noon. The FPS counter in the corner dips in these captures because the script had just teleported the camera; steady-state numbers are in the frame budget below.

More from the new renderer

These scenes weren't in the audit set.

How a frame is drawn

These stages run in order every frame.

  1. Sky tableA physically based Rayleigh, Mie and ozone sky is rendered into a 256×128 lookup table whenever the time of day moves. The same model runs on the CPU and gives the sun colour, the ambient light and the fog colour.
  2. Shadow cascadesFour 2048² cascades in one depth atlas, split at 10, 28, 72 and 190 m. Each cascade is snapped to its texel grid so edges don't crawl as you walk.
  3. SceneForward shading with GGX highlights, soft wrap lighting and translucency for leaves, and up to 16 lamps and campfires. Direct and ambient light go to separate HDR targets, so ambient occlusion only darkens what it should.
  4. Sky and cloudsDrawn after solid geometry: sun and moon discs, twinkling stars, the milky way and a cloud layer lit by the sun or the moon. The same cloud field casts moving shadows on the ground.
  5. Water and effectsWater refracts a copy of the scene with depth-based absorption and reflects the sky. Campfire flames, snow and falling leaves draw afterwards.
  6. Light and airHalf-resolution ambient occlusion and a 32-step march for light shafts through the haze, each with an edge-preserving blur.
  7. FinishSix-level bloom, AgX tone mapping with a gentle grade and a blue shift at night, FXAA, then the HUD.

Frame budget

Castle courtyard at noon, uncapped, averaged over the steady state. Each section waits for the GPU before its timer stops, so the total runs a little above a normal frame.

16.7 ms · 60 FPS
  • Frame setup0.27 ms
  • Shadow cascades6.33 ms
  • Opaque scene8.11 ms
  • Sky and transparents1.15 ms
  • Post-processing2.29 ms
  • HUD0.91 ms
  • Present0.46 ms
  • Total19.52 ms

The dense wilderness forest, with 2,000+ instanced trees, runs at 48–57 FPS uncapped under the same profiling. Grass chunks, trees and rocks are instanced, so draw calls stay flat as the world fills up.
